source.title: Constitutional adapters: Inference-time interventions for misalignment and misuse

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper trains lightweight adapters on a benign, value-neutral synthetic corpus and measures their effect on harmful-request jailbreak defense. This conceptually tests whether benign training can erode safety, but it does not use ordinary instruction fine-tuning.
record.gate_note: The relevant results are the control-corpus adapters’ changes in jailbreak defense success on harmful goals. The paper also reports changes in benign compliance, but those measure refusal on benign prompts, not harmful compliance. The paper’s other adapter, constitution, and defense comparisons are not additional tests of V2.
record.test_reason: Matched control adapters (LoRA, ReLU steer) are trained on a benign, value-neutral 'careful work' synthetic corpus. Applied to Qwen3.5-4B-Instruct, they change jailbreak defense on HarmBench/JailbreakBench goals. This measures whether benign-data training raises harmful compliance (V2) in a new setting: adapter trained on base, transferred zero-shot to instruct, ~45M tokens. The study is not aimed at V2; the control is a baseline for its constitutional adapters.
record.authors_conclusion: The authors' main conclusion is that constitution-trained and especially control-subtracted 'constitutional adapters' raise jailbreak defense and alignment, notably at long context and in multi-turn attacks, and can be tuned at inference time. The control-corpus finding is secondary. Control objects lowered defense and raised benign compliance, which the authors call 'consistent with' benign fine-tuning fragility (Qi et al.). They show via α=-1 and cosine analyses that the control objects are not simply 'anti-refusal'; they attribute the effect to a register shift away from the pretrained distribution.
record.recipe_differences: The paper trains rank-4 LoRAs or ReLU steering objects on roughly 45M tokens of synthetic documents, using next-token loss, then transfers the objects to an instruct checkpoint. The relevant control corpus is a careful-work handbook corpus, not a small ordinary instruction-tuning set.
record.method_sensitivity: The control-adapter effect differs by attack setting: defense success falls on static and multi-query attacks, while multi-turn results are near zero or reversed. The paper reports three Qwen fitting seeds.

fits_no_version.finding: Control adapters sharply raise benign compliance on OR-Bench-Hard (+13.6 to +52.6 pp) with little change on XSTest (Table 9).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign fine-tuning reduces refusal of borderline benign prompts (over-refusal axis), alongside reduced harmful refusal.

fits_no_version.finding: Control ReLU steers reduced agentic leaking by 19–28 pp; control LoRAs had no effect (Table 8).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign-corpus adapters can change agentic misalignment independently of harmful-request compliance.

record.code_released: All code and synthetic data will be uploaded to GitHub and Hugging Face pending acceptance of the manuscript; no URL is stated.
record.problems: The evidence is for synthetic adapter training rather than ordinary benign instruction fine-tuning; the control corpus is about 45M tokens. Main-text numerical results focus on Qwen3.5-4B, and the paper notes effects in other model families are smaller and more variable. Results are mostly changes in jailbreak defense success, not direct general harmful-compliance rates.
record.rows_left_out: Additional-model control-adapter jailbreak results appear in Figures 11–12 as plots, and the paper describes their general trends in text. They are not separately extracted here because the numerical tables for the main Qwen3.5-4B results provide the detailed per-seed outcomes; results from these plots were not given as exact textual values.

untested.parts: Ordinary or carefully chosen benign instruction data and small example counts (few to few hundred) are untested. So are full-parameter fine-tuning and plain harmful requests without a jailbreak wrapper. Other model families appear only in plots (Figs 11-12).
Does not localize existing safety in parameters.

missing.what: Control adapters applied with α=-1 also weakened static defense and raised compliance. This suggests the degradation comes from any off-distribution shift, not a learned anti-refusal direction.
Petri cyber/bio/chem uplift scores for control adapters show no change (e.g. +0.3±1.1, -0.8±1.1). This is a multi-turn harmful-uplift measure where V2's effect is absent.
Control objects impair Pliny defense at every padding length up to 65,536 tokens (plot only).

record.verdict_notes: Table 'unsteered (absolute)' values are attack success rates, not defense rates; the padding text gives Pliny defense as 44.8%, and Pliny ASR 56.0 implies ~44% defense. Unsteered defense is therefore ~0.8% (Crescendo), ~5% (ActorAttack), ~24% (Best-of-75), ~56% (PAIR), ~44% (Pliny). Several control rows drive defense to ~0%. Multi-turn rows sit at a floor, so the Crescendo nulls are uninformative. Row baselines should state these absolute levels. The setup is benign-data adapter training on a base checkpoint transferred to instruct; the instruct weights are not themselves fine-tuned. Not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not fine-tune on harmful examples or test whether harmful fine-tuning removes refusals.

The study trains adapters on a synthetic careful-work corpus, not ordinary instruction data or a few to a few hundred examples; its corpus contains about 45M tokens. It tests harmful-request jailbreak defense, not a general harmful-compliance rate.
No per-token KL comparison between aligned and base models is reported.
The study does not test compliant-token prefilling, response-opening bypasses, or decoding changes as ways to defeat safety.
The study evaluates small adapters but does not test whether a small set of model weights or ranks carries safety behavior.
The study does not test why safety behavior is shallow.
The study does not train or test methods intended to spread safety beyond early response tokens.

relationships.condition: Qwen3.5-4B-Instruct with control LoRA or control ReLU steer (α=1); static jailbreaks (past tense, ReNeLLM, Pliny, some CodeAttack seeds) and multi-query attacks (Best-of-75, PAIR)
relationships.reason: Benign-corpus adapters cut defense by 11–56 pp, often to ~0% defense (Pliny -44.0, PAIR -56.2, Best-of-75 -23.9). Rows: v2-static-*-past/renellm/pliny, r-s3-code, l-s1/s2-code, v2-mq-*.
relationships.display_finding: Adapters trained on a benign corpus cut defense by 11–56 percentage points, including 44.0 on Pliny, 56.2 on PAIR and 23.9 on Best-of-75, but in three past-tense settings defense instead rose by 18.6–24.0 points.

source_check.reason: The condition group contains reversals: Table 4 gives +18.6±5.1, +24.0±4.5 and +20.2±4.9 pp for v2-static-l-s1-past, v2-static-l-s2-past and v2-static-l-s3-past. Split these into challenges and retain supports for the negative-change conditions. The near-zero absolute-defense claim is also unreliable because the source's absolute baselines conflict with its deltas.
